rpy-parity-d1f65c8c0.text: `python/cpp/bindings_proportion.cpp::fast_zero_one_inflated_beta` (return_mismatch): The R export `fast_zero_one_inflated_beta_cpp` takes `estimate_only = false`. Unless `estimate_only` is TRUE, it also returns `vcov`, the joint covariance. It also returns `b`, `log_phi`, `zero_one_b0` and `zero_one_b1` as separate fields. The Python binding has no `estimate_only` argument. It returns only `params`, `neg_loglik`, `num_iter`, `hit_iteration_cap`, `converged` and `gradient_norm`. It never computes or returns a covariance matrix or Hessian. The docstring does not say the variance is omitted. A Python user therefore cannot reproduce the R standard errors from this binding. Separately, the docstring describes `fixed_idx` only as "Optional indices of fixed parameters." The R roxygen says it is 1-indexed into [beta, log_phi, gamma_0, gamma_1], and the kernel's `make_fixed_param_spec` treats it that way. The Python text does not state this. Suggested: Decide whether the Python binding should expose the covariance. If so, add an `estimate_only` argument and a `vcov` return field, as `fast_coxph_regression` does. If not, say in the docstring that no variance is returned and that `estimate_only` is not supported. Also document that `fixed_idx` is 1-based into [beta, log_phi, zero_one_inflation_params]. I did not give a docstring fix for that sentence. The text "Optional indices of fixed parameters." probably also appears in the `fast_beta_regression` docstring in the same file, so it is not unique.

The Python binding has no such arguments. It hard-codes `std::nullopt, std::nullopt` for them in the call to `fast_clogit_plus_glmm_internal`, and the docstring does not say so. A Python user cannot reproduce the R weighted fit, which changes results. Suggested: Add optional `weights_disc` and `weights_conc` py::args to the binding and pass them through to the kernel. If the omission is intended, add a docstring sentence saying the binding always fits unweighted.
